method: Actual BoardStream controller with a Node fetch SSE adapter, one connection at a time. Five rounds per league; each receives an initial complete snapshot, deliberately closes only its own viewer connection, then uses the configured250ms client retry and receives a new full snapshot. Finally hold one college stream for30s. Monotonic timestamps are public HTTP/SSE receipt times, not browser paint or bookmaker latency.
limits: No provider connection, deployment, service or extra-market panel was restarted. Only own viewer connections were closed.
Source accuracy beyond snapshot integrity is checked separately.
Observed only this bounded window and one network location.
Controlled reconnect includes250ms scheduled client delay; does not measure recovery from a real upstream bookmaker failure.

fanduel.transport: Live push with independent league verification

notes: Browser samples are client-reported estimates after two animation frames, corrected using /api/time. Inspect clock uncertainty.
DraftKings createdTime is the provider feed timestamp, not a verified trading-engine change timestamp. Cross-host clock skew can affect it.
FanDuel push updatedAt has whole-second precision. Its age is an upper-bound estimate with up to about 999ms quantization plus unmeasured provider clock skew; HTTP prices have no change timestamp.

FanDuel uses immediate push alongside configured HTTP checks, continuing HTTP if push is unavailable. Nominal polling wait averages half the interval only for uniformly timed changes without delays; this is not a measured end-to-end guarantee or a maximum price age.
Live rows with n=0 mean not measured; pregame results must not be presented as live results.

history.note: Actual server observations only. History can be shorter than the selected window after startup, gaps, or capacity eviction. Restored history never restores live eligibility.

storage.message: Historical observations only; restored data never makes a live price eligible.
